methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target the technology gap through peer-to-peer skill building in a non-metro region, signaling grassroots distribution of foundational AI literacy beyond traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and AI education capacity in Richmond Metro, potentially deepening capabilities in the state capital while leaving rural adjacencies unserved.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents distributed institutional investment in AI workforce preparation outside major metros, creating potential node for deep learning in traditionally underserved Southwest Virginia if sustained beyond initial launch.

signals.title: DC and Northern Virginia: Your guide to coding and AI upskilling programs - Technical.ly
signals.signal_reading: Coding and AI upskilling programs in DC/NoVA concentrate platform-mediated training opportunities in the existing tech corridor, likely producing broad but shallow adoption that reinforces rather than redistributes existing advantages.

signals.title: VT Science Corner: Designing better battery technology with X-rays and AI - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's advanced battery research using AI and X-rays demonstrates deep technical capability in New River Valley, but concentration in university research context may not translate to broader regional workforce AI fluency.
